To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• The generalization ability of a linear prediction algorithm can be characterized by the uniform convergence rates and covering numbers of its weight space, and that these rates can be bounded by the Rademacher and/or Gaussian complexities of the weight space.

1. For the case of linear predictors with Lp norm constraints on the weight vectors, the uniform convergence rates are the same as the regret bounds of the online gradient descent algorithm (with L2 loss), and the regret bounds of follow the leader (with L1 loss).

(1) the uniform convergence rates for empirical risk minimization for linear prediction tightly match the regret rates of online learning algorithms (up to a constant factor), and (2) the uniform convergence rate for linear prediction is independent of the dimension of the data, provided the L2 norm is constrained.
